evidence: This is the thesis disclosing its own confound, and the directional argument is sound and explicitly hedged (twopool.tex sec sim-limitations). Mechanism: the sim sets the language prefill length to the trace's ContextTokens verbatim, which embeds the TRACED model's vision tokenization (~66 tok/image, per trace-eda chapter) — roughly 3x below a Qwen3-VL-consistent 196-per-image prefill — so frames-class language work is undercounted, making the language pool look better in bursts. Conversely the uniform 448^2 assumption costs a full forward per image, overstating frames-class encoder work (small frames-class images would cost less), making the vision pool look worse. Both biases push the SAME direction as the observed burst asymmetry (language removable floor vs vision hard queueing). The claim is a signed-bias reasoning statement, not a precision result; it is correctly labelled 'convention-dependent' with a 'both-conventions sensitivity run remains future work' caveat. Appropriately hedged confound disclosure.
